content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in New Haven

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires specific education and project-management experience before you apply. Review PMI's eligibility criteria—secondary degree holders and bachelor's-degree holders face different experience thresholds. Gather documentation of your work history to verify you meet PMI's baseline requirements.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led PMP Boot Camp. Our synchronous sessions deliver PMI-required formal education on demand, designed for New Haven professionals balancing work and study. You'll cover the PMBOK® Guide framework and real-world applications across five process groups.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After training, submit your PMP application directly to PMI through their online portal. Include your education credentials, work experience hours, and proof of completion from Granite PM Academy. Pay the exam fee and await PMI's eligibility review—typically completed within days.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Sit for the Exam
steps_items.text: Granite PM Academy provides exam-preparation resources, practice questions, and study guides to reinforce your learning. The PMP exam is computer-delivered and proctored. Schedule your test at a PMI-authorized testing center and apply the knowledge you gained in your boot camp to earn your credential.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP Credential
steps_items.text: After you pass, you'll enter PMI's three-year renewal cycle. Earn professional development units (PDUs) through training, volunteer work, and project leadership to maintain active status. Renew before your credential expires to keep the PMP designation current on your resume.
